spans.s: दुष् vi. 4P (pp. दुष्ट; pres. दुष्यति) 1. To be corrupted, to be soiled, to suffer damage; 2. to be defiled or violated, to be impure, M.x.102, vii.24; 3. to sin, to commit a mistake, to be wrong; 4. to be unchaste, to be faithless.With प्र-, 1. to be corrupted, to be soiled; 2. to sin, to be unchaste, M.ix.74, Bg.i.40.

दुष् Caus. (दूषयति-ते, also दोषयति when the root means ‘to be depraved’) 1. to corrupt, to soil, to cause to perish, to defile, to vitiate, to taint, M.vii.105, R.xii.4, viii.68, x.47; 2. to violate, to break, न त्वेवं दूषयिष्यामि शस्त्रग्रहमहाव्रतम् Mv.iii.; to violate a maiden, M.viii.364; 3. to deprave, to demoralize; 4. to adulterate; 5. to rescind, to abrogate; 6. to find fault with, to speak ill of, to censure, e.g. दूषितः सर्वलोकेषु निषादत्व गमिष्यति &c.)With प्र-, 1. to spoil, to soil, R.xi.25; 2. to censure, to find fault with.With सम्-, 1. to corrupt, to soil, to taint; 2. to find fault with, to censure; 3. to violate.
दुस् ind. A prefix to nouns and rarely to verbs implying ‘evil, bad, wicked, hard, difficult, inferior &c.’
दुष्ट a. (f. ष्टा) 1. Spoiled, injured, damaged; 2. depraved; 3. vicious, wicked; 4. faulty, guilty; 5. low, vile; 6. worthless; 7. defective (as a hetu); 8. painful.
दुष्ट a. (f. ष्टा) 1. Spoiled, injured, damaged; 2. depraved; 3. vicious, wicked; 4. faulty, guilty; 5. low, vile; 6. worthless; 7. defective (as a hetu); 8. painful.
दुष्ट-आत्मन्, -आशय a. evil-minded, wicked.
दुष्ट-आत्मन्, -आशय a. evil-minded, wicked.
दुष्ट-गज m. a vicious elephant.
दुष्ट-चेतस्, -धी, -बुद्धि a. evil-intentioned, wicked.

दुष्ट-वृष m. a strong but stubborn ox which refuses to draw.
दुष्टि f. Corruption, depravity.
दुष्टु ind. 1. Ill, bad; 2. improperly, incorrectly.
दुष्कर (I) a. hard to be accomplished, difficult, arduous, मुग्धे दुष्करमेतत् Am.
, M.vii.55.
दुष्कर (II) n. 1. a difficult or painful task, a difficulty; 2. atmosphere, æther.

दुष्काल m. 1. bad times; 2. the time of universal destruction; 3. an epithet of Śiva.
दुष्कुल n. low family, (आददीत) स्त्रीरत्नं दुष्कुलादपि M.ii.238.
दुष्कुलीन a. low-born.
दुष्कृत् m. a wicked person.
दुष्कृत n. sin, misdeed, उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते Bg.ii.50.
दुष्कृति f. sin, misdeed, उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते Bg.ii.50.
दुष्क्रम a. ill-arranged, unmethodical.
दुश्चर (I) a. 1. inaccessible; 2. difficult to be performed or accomplished, R.viii.79, K.S.vii.65; 3. acting ill, behaving wickedly.
दुश्चर (II) m. 1. a bear; 2. a bi-valve shell.
दुश्चरित (I) a. wicked, abandoned.
दुश्चरित (II) n. misbehaviour, ill conduct.

दुश्च्यवन m. an epithet of Indra.
दुश्च्याव m. an epithet of Śiva.
दुष्टर a. 1. difficult to be crossed, R.i.2, M.iv.242; 2. difficult to be subdued, invincible.
दुष्टर a. 1. difficult to be crossed, R.i.2, M.iv.242; 2. difficult to be subdued, invincible.

दुःपच a. difficult to be digested.
दुष्पतन n. an abusive epithet.

दुष्प्रकृति a. bad-tempered, evil-natured.
दुष्प्रजस् a. having bad offspring.
दुःप्रज्ञ a. weak-minded, stupid.

दुष्प्रधर्ष a. See दुर्धर्ष, R.ii.27.

दुष्प्रवृत्ति f. bad news, R.xii.51.
दुःप्रसह a. 1. irresistible, terrible; 2. hard to endure.
दुष्प्राप a. unattainable, Bg.vi.36, R.i.48.
दुष्प्राप a. unattainable, Bg.vi.36, R.i.48.

दुःसह a. unbearable, irresistible.

दूष a. (f. षा) (at the end of a compound) Defiling, polluting, e.g. पंक्तिदूष.

दूषक a. (f. षिका) 1. Corrupting, polluting, spoiling; 2. violating, dishonouring, seducing; 3. offending, trespassing; 4. disfiguring; 5. sinful, wicked (as an action).

दूषिका f. 1. A pencil, a paintbrush; 2. a kind of rice.

दूषण (I) n. 1. The act of spoiling, corrupting, ruining, vitiating; 2. violating, breaking (an agreement); 3. dishonouring (a woman); 4. slighting, abusing, detracting, blame, censure, R.xii.46; 5. objection, adverse argument; 6. fault, defect, sin, offence, वैदेह्याः पर गृहवासदूषणं यत् Ut.i., M.ii.213.
दूषण (II) m. Name of a Rākṣasa killed by Rāma, R.xii.46.
दूषण-अरि m. an epithet of Rāma.
